title: Acid, base or neither?
body: Acids make lemon juice and vinegar taste sour. Bases, like soap and baking soda in water, feel slippery. Plain water is neither, so we call it neutral. Some cleaners are acids, and many are bases. So cleaning or stinging won't tell you which.
Scientists use pH to say how acidic something is. It's a number that usually runs from 0 to 14. Below 7 is an acid. Exactly 7 is neutral. Above 7 is a base.
Red cabbage juice is an indicator, a dye that changes colour. It turns pink or red in acids. It stays purple when a liquid is neutral. In bases, it turns blue and then green.
realWorld: Your stomach uses strong acid to break down food. Heartburn tablets, called antacids, are bases that cancel out the extra acid. Gardeners test their soil too, because blueberries grow best in acidic soil.
